newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 30.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** A week-long nationwide strike by postal and telecommunication employees called off after government lifts ceiling on bonus payments
** Former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao to appear before New Delhi court to face criminal charges in seven-year old forgery case
** Securities and Exchange Board of India approves expansion of Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) to other cities
** The market regulator reduces minimum new issue application lots to 200 shares from 500 to lure sulking retail investors
** Finance Minister P. Chidambaram says fiscal deficit would be kept on target at 5.0 percent of gross domestic product, the Economic Times reports
** The Indian rupee INR= opened steady at 35.65/66 per dollar. Dealers expect strong month-end demand for dollars to continue
MARKETS:
** On Tuesday, Indian shares drifted lower in sluggish trade with domestic and foreign funds booking profits at last week's sharp rally
The 30-share BSE index dropped 24.58 points, or 0.75 percent, to 3,239.94 The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index lost 9.50 points, or 1.01 percent, to 926.39.
The 500-share CRISIL index shed 4.97 points, or 0.80 percent, to 619.76.
STOCKS TO WATCH:
** Sandoz fell 46 rupees, or 14.98 percent, to 261 on Tuesday, hit by an "unfavourable" stocks swap merger ratio with Hindustan Ciba-Geigy
Sandoz said on Monday it will offer its shareholders 10
shares in Hindustan Ciba-Geigy in exchange for every 17 shares they hold in Sandoz India.
Hindustan Ciba-Geigy rose 416.25 rupees, or 17.67
percent to 2,771.25
** Thermax Ltd is scheduled to release its first half results. The boiler/cooler maker stock ended 3.25 rupees higher at 346 on Tuesday
** Crompton Greaves said Tuesday its net profit in the first six months to September 30, 1996 fell to 160.5 million rupees against 239.4 million in the year-ago period
Sales were higher at 6.13 billion rupees against 5.52
billion. The share lost 3.0 rupees to 154.50 on Tuesday
